_about: Truth/prior orbital elements for the S301 + friends joint fit. Angles in deg, a in mas, t_p and element_epoch in decimal Julian years. Errors are the published formal 1-sigma. Angle convention: Gillessen et al. 2009 (observer frame x = +Dec (north), y = +RA (east), z = away from observer; Omega counted from north through east; ascending node = where the star crosses the sky plane moving away from us; i > 90 deg = clockwise on the sky). This is the frame of relatipy's KerrMcmcModel (axes (Dec, RA, away)), verified in validation.md. element_epoch = osculation epoch at which the Kepler elements are converted to the initial state of the integration.

global.source: GRAVITY Collaboration 2024, A&A 692 A242 (arXiv:2409.12261), Table B.1, four-star fit

alternative.source: GRAVITY 2022 values used (fixed) for the S301 discovery fit (arXiv:2607.12664 p.6; errors from arXiv:2609.06936 p.2)

frame_offsets_naco_gravity2024.note: NACO reference-frame parameters of the GRAVITY 2024 fit. Not applied to the mocks (mocks are generated in the Sgr A* frame).

S301A.element_epoch_note: Osculation epoch not stated in the paper. We use the preceding apocentre t_p - P/2 (P = 8.682 yr from a, M, R0), as GRAVITY 2024 does for S2 (2010.35) and S29 (1977). Any epoch 2017-2022.9 fits the digitized points about equally (chi2 within ~3); any epoch after the 2023.13 pericentre is rejected (RMS 3 mas, chi2 ~6000): the osculating omega jumps by the ~2 deg Schwarzschild precession across pericentre. See validation.md.
S301A.source: GRAVITY Collaboration 2026, Nature (arXiv:2607.12664), Extended Data Table 2, first value/error pair (= solution A; adopted by arXiv:2609.06936 and by Ext. Data Fig. 5)

S301B.source: arXiv:2607.12664 Extended Data Table 2, second value/error pair (= solution B). Main text p.6 quotes e = 0.9821 for B; the table gives 0.9824 (table value used).
S301B.mirror_note: Solution B is essentially the z-mirror of A: Omega_B - Omega_A = 183.1 deg and omega_B - omega_A = -178.3 deg (both ~180 deg), with i, e, a, t_p equal within errors. (Omega, omega) -> (Omega + 180, omega + 180) leaves the sky-projected Keplerian orbit unchanged and flips the line-of-sight coordinate z -> -z, hence the sign of the radial velocity. Astrometry alone cannot separate A and B (chi2 25.86 vs 25.53); radial velocities break the degeneracy (Romer delay could in principle but does not yet). Spin effects (Lense-Thirring) are not mirror symmetric either unless the spin is mirrored too.

S2.source: GRAVITY Collaboration 2024 (arXiv:2409.12261) Table B.1; elements osculating at 2010.35 (table caption)
